pr.title: Fold pointer operations in GVN
pr.description:
This PR proposes 2 combinations of cast operations in MIR GVN:
- a chain of `PtrToPtr` or `MutToConstPointer` casts can be folded together into a single `PtrToPtr` cast;
- we attempt to evaluate more ptr ops when there is no provenance.

In particular, this allows to read from static slices.

This is not yet sufficient to see through slice operations that use `PtrComponents` (because that's a union), but still a step forward.

r? @ghost

processing.reason:
The only historically incorrect transformation identified in the PR history is DataflowConstProp's removed pointer-arithmetic branch: for `Add | Sub | BitOr | BitAnd | BitXor` on two pointer operands it folded by extracting the LHS pointer, operating on `usize` addresses, and rebuilding `Pointer::new(ptr.provenance, ...)`. That branch is not reachable from source-grounded MIR: ordinary Rust does not emit a `BinOp` with two raw-pointer operands. Pointer-plus-integer arithmetic is the separate MIR `BinOp::Offset`, which `InterpCx::binary_ptr_op` handles before the machine hook (with pointee-size scaling and bounds checks), and `ptr as usize + n` is an integer operation. Thus no function pair using the PR's actual input domain can trigger the historical rewrite while also passing Miri; reaching it would require inventing an unreachable MIR operation.

The reachable PR transformations are (a) GVN folding consecutive `PtrToPtr`/`MutToConstPointer` casts, (b) GVN evaluating unsizing and pointer-to-pointer casts, and (c) DataflowConstProp folding provenance-free pointer comparisons. I checked (c) concretely with `test_program_pair` on the PR's own `wide_ptr_integer` witness: transmuted wide pointers `(1,1)` and `(1,2)` compared at runtime under Miri and the PR's lexicographic bit fold both produced the same bitmask 14 for `==/!=/</<=/>/>=`, with O0/O3 agreeing. Cast-chain folding and unsize evaluation likewise preserve the data address and metadata as shown by the PR's MIR diffs. Encoding an address-only comparison fold or a byte-vs-element pointer-arithmetic difference would be a different, invented rewrite rather than the historical one, which the task forbids.

analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, GVN's `Rvalue::Cast` handling simplified the operand and then built `Value::Cast { kind, value, from, to }`; chained `PtrToPtr`/`PointerCoercion(MutToConstPointer)` casts therefore remained separate MIR casts, and the GVN evaluator did not evaluate unsizing or pointer-to-pointer casts. DataflowConstProp's `DummyMachine::binary_ptr_op` unconditionally did `throw_machine_stop_str!(\"can't do pointer arithmetic\");`, so pointer comparisons were never const-propagated.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The PR's intermediate implementation evaluated pointer arithmetic in DataflowConstProp: for `Add | Sub | BitOr | BitAnd | BitXor` it extracted the LHS pointer, did the operation on `usize`, and rebuilt `Pointer::new(ptr.provenance, ...)`. Patch 7 removed that branch and replaced it with `throw_machine_stop_str!(\"pointer arithmetic is not handled\")` under the subject `Remove untested arithmetic ops.` So the incorrect rewrite is to const-fold pointer arithmetic rather than only provenance-free pointer comparisons. Separately, a cast-chain fold must not merge reification casts, and pointer comparisons must bail when provenance makes `to_bits` fail.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR containing pointer casts and pointer comparisons: chains of `*const T`/`*mut T` casts (`PtrToPtr`, `PointerCoercion(MutToConstPointer)`), unsizing coercions to slices/trait objects, wide pointers built via `transmute((usize, usize))`, comparisons `== != < <= > >=`, and constant slice indexing such as `(&[1u32, 2, 3] as &[u32])[1]`. Provenance-carrying pointers and pointer arithmetic form the excluded/limited cases.
analysis.summary: GVN now folds consecutive pointer casts into one `PtrToPtr` cast, evaluates unsizing and pointer-to-pointer casts, and DataflowConstProp evaluates pointer comparisons only when there is no provenance. The PR deliberately does not evaluate pointer arithmetic in const-prop, and does not simplify comparisons where provenance is present.
analysis.trigger: GVN sees consecutive pointer casts or an unsize/pointer cast whose operand is already a constant; DataflowConstProp sees a pointer comparison. DataflowConstProp only folds the comparison when the operands have no provenance.
preconditions: Both casts in the chain are `PtrToPtr` or `PointerCoercion(MutToConstPointer)`; the collapsed cast is emitted as `PtrToPtr`.
If the inner source type equals the outer destination type, the cast is dropped and the inner value is returned.
`ReifyFnPointer` and `ClosureFnPointer(_)` remain opaque and must never be merged, because each reification may produce a different pointer.
Pointer comparisons use `to_bits`; if either pointer has provenance, `to_bits` returns `Err` and the fold bails out.
Unsize evaluation allocates a destination and marks that allocation immutable.
DataflowConstProp stops interpretation rather than computing pointer arithmetic.
pitfalls: Do not fold comparisons of provenance-carrying pointers even when both point into the same allocation; the `wide_ptr_same_provenance` test expects the `Eq`/`Ne`/`Lt`/`Le`/`Gt`/`Ge` operations to remain.
Do not equate pointer comparison with ordinary integer comparison: wide pointers are `ScalarPair`s compared lexicographically by bits, and scalar operands are padded with zero.
Do not evaluate pointer arithmetic merely because pointer comparisons are evaluable; patch 7 explicitly removed `Add/Sub/BitOr/BitAnd/BitXor` as untested.
Only combine pointer casts in a chain; reification of generic function pointers may yield different pointers and must stay opaque.
`PtrComponents` is a union, so this optimization does not yet see through slice operations that use it.
A retained test name or old comment is not evidence that the old transformation is correct; compare the actual value assignments in the emitted MIR.
analysis.testStrategy: Use MIR-opt tests that emit GVN and DataflowConstProp diffs. In `tests/mir-opt/gvn.rs`, keep separate functions for provenance (`wide_ptr_provenance`, `wide_ptr_same_provenance`) and provenance-free (`wide_ptr_integer`) pointer operations; CHECK that provenance cases retain `Eq`/`Ne`/... while the integer case becomes `opaque::<bool>(const false)` / `opaque::<bool>(const true)`. Use `transmute((usize, usize))` to construct wide pointers without provenance. In `const_prop/slice_len.rs`, CHECK for `assert(const true,` and `[[a]] = const 2_u32;`. In dataflow-const-prop `default_boxed_slice`, CHECK for `const Box::<[bool]>(`. Also add a no-ICE test for provenance-free wide-pointer comparisons.
